items.page_hint: Event-level call ledger / Derived totals — 'Processed (100% prefix reuse)' bullet
items.issue: The bullet uses 865 = δ + γ per turn as the re-processed count under 100% prefix reuse, yielding 11,795 input tokens. However, the W_reuse formula in the same section correctly states 'only the incremental prefix (9,200 + 3×800 = 11,600 — the γ reasoning tokens were generated in the prior call, so their KV already exists) is pre-filled.' Under prefix reuse, γ tokens' KV is created during the prior call's decode and does not need re-processing; only the δ tool-output tokens (800/turn) require new prefill. The correct re-processed input is 9,200 + 3×800 = 11,600, not 11,795. The corrected total would be 11,600 + 495 = 12,095 (which conveniently equals the peak residency, confirming every token is processed exactly once under full prefix reuse).
items.quoted_clause: only each call's newly appended tokens are re-processed, 9,200 + 3 × 865 = **11,795** input + 495 output = **12,290** tokens
items.fix_instruction: Change the bullet to 'only each call's newly appended tokens whose KV does not yet exist are re-processed, 9,200 + 3 × 800 = **11,600** input + 495 output = **12,095** tokens', with a parenthetical that γ's KV already exists from the prior call's decode (consistent with the W_reuse formula).
items.evidence: chapter-19.md contains verbatim: '- **Processed (100% prefix reuse)**: only each call's newly appended tokens are re-processed, 9,200 + 3 × 865 = **11,795** input + 495 output = **12,290** tokens.' Same section states: 'only the incremental prefix (9,200 + 3×800 = 11,600 — the γ reasoning tokens were generated in the prior call, so their KV already exists) is pre-filled, giving W_reuse(3) ≈ 14.14 s.' Arithmetic rechecked: 9200+3*865=11795; 9200+3*800=11600; difference 195=3*65 (γ). Ledger's final retained context is 12,095, matching the corrected total. Two definitions of 're-processed' coexist in one section.

items.issue: The definition lists three additive components: retained history, new retrieval δ, and prompt. In the ledger's convention, retrieval/tool output occurs AFTER the model call, so there is no 'new retrieval δ' in any call's input — the example confirms this (call-2 input = 9,200 + 865 = 10,065, with no separate δ term). A reader could interpret 'new retrieval δ' as the prior turn's tool output (which IS part of retained_history), leading to double-counting: 865 + 800 + 9,200 = 10,865 ≠ 10,065. The definition is either describing a different calling convention (retrieval-before-model-call) without saying so, or the δ term is always zero in this context and should be removed or explicitly noted as zero.
items.quoted_clause: the full input of a given call (retained history + new retrieval δ + prompt)
items.fix_instruction: Either remove 'new retrieval δ' from the definition and note that in the ledger's convention retrieval arrives after the model call, or qualify it: 'new retrieval δ (zero in the ledger's post-call retrieval convention; nonzero if the system retrieves before the model call).'
items.evidence: chapter-19.md definitions table verbatim: '| current_input_length | the full input of a given call (retained history + new retrieval δ + prompt) | call-2 input = 9,200 + 865 = 10,065 ...' — the example has no separate δ term. retained_history row: 'call 2 carries 10,065 − 9,200 = 865 prior-turn tokens (δ₁ + γ₁)'. Event ledger columns run Call → New model output → Tool output, i.e. tool output arrives AFTER the call, so no call input contains a new δ; δ₁ is already inside the 865. Definition lists three additive components the example never uses; double-count reading (865+800+9,200=10,865≠10,065) is possible.

items.page_hint: Multi-step reasoning cost — β discussion vs W_reuse formula
items.issue: W_reuse(3) is stated as ≈ 14.14 s in the W formula section but as ~14.16 s in the β/task-multiplier discussion. The correct value from the stated inputs is 14.14 s: (11,600/9,200)×1.08 + 12.375 + 0.399 = 1.362 + 12.375 + 0.399 = 14.136 ≈ 14.14. The 14.16 s value is obtained by using 11,795 (the incorrect prefill count from AGT-01): (11,795/9,200)×1.08 + 12.375 + 0.399 = 14.159 ≈ 14.16. This also affects the stated multiplier: 14.14/8.58 = 1.648 ≈ 1.65× (correct with exact base 8.58), but 14.16/8.6 = 1.647 ≈ 1.65× (coincidentally also 1.65× with rounded base). The time value itself is inconsistent.
items.quoted_clause: (to ~14.16 s / ~1.65× with 100% prefix reuse, a full increase of ~5.6 s)
items.fix_instruction: Change '~14.16 s' to '~14.14 s' in the β/task-multiplier discussion (and the other 14.16 occurrences) so W_reuse(3) reads 14.14 s in all locations; keep 1.65× only if the base is stated as 8.58.
items.evidence: chapter-19.md contains verbatim '(to ~14.16 s / ~1.65× with 100% prefix reuse, a full increase of ~5.6 s)' (plus '~14.16 s with prefix reuse' and '~10.44 s / ~14.16 s under 100% prefix reuse' — three 14.16 occurrences), while the W_reuse formula states 'W_reuse(3) ≈ 14.14 s' (one occurrence). Recomputed: (11600/9200)*1.08+12.375+0.399 = 14.136 ≈ 14.14; (11795/9200)*1.08+12.375+0.399 = 14.159 ≈ 14.16. The 14.16 value comes from the 11,795 prefill count; 14.14/8.58 = 1.648 ≈ 1.65×.

items.issue: 'This' refers to L_base ≈ 8.6 s (1.08 s prefill + 7.5 s decode of 300 tokens). The intermediate reasoning is T×65 tokens, costing T×1.625 s of decode — far less than a full 8.6 s. A reader could conclude the full 8.6 s is paid twice (once for the final answer, once for intermediate reasoning), which would be incorrect. The intermediate reasoning adds decode time for γ tokens plus prefill of the grown prefix, not another full L_base.
items.quoted_clause: Every agentic request pays this at least once, and usually again for the intermediate reasoning the loop generates (the T·γ tokens).
items.fix_instruction: Reword to: 'Every agentic request pays L_base at least once for the final answer, and pays additional decode time for the intermediate reasoning the loop generates (the T·γ tokens, ~1.6 s per turn at ~25 ms/token)' so a reader cannot conclude the full 8.6 s is paid twice.
items.evidence: chapter-19.md verbatim: 'Base inference latency *L*base — ... ~8.6 s: 1.08 s prefill (Ch 8) + ~7.5 s decode of the 300-token answer at ~25 ms/token (Ch 8). Every agentic request pays this at least once, and usually again for the intermediate reasoning the loop generates (the T·γ tokens).' 'This' grammatically refers to the ~8.6 s L_base just defined, but the T·γ tokens cost T×65×25 ms = 4.875 s decode at T=3 (the W formula separates these components), not another 8.6 s. The arithmetic in the finding (T×1.625 s vs 8.6 s) checks out.

items.issue: λ_step is described as an 'average' (~120 ms) while λ_tool is described as a 'median' (~100 ms), but L_agent is claimed to be a 'median' (~220 ms). The sum of an average and a median is not necessarily a median (median(X+Y) ≠ median(X) + median(Y) in general). The text mixes statistical terms for components of the same sum.
items.quoted_clause: the per-turn agent step averages ~120 ms ... λ_tool ≈ 100 ms (median, tool backend) ... So per-turn orchestration overhead L_agent ≈ 220 ms (median).
items.fix_instruction: Use one statistical term consistently: 'average' for λ_step, λ_tool and L_agent (≈220 ms average), or 'median' for all three if the 120 ms figure is also a median, or reword L_agent to '≈ 220 ms (typical/central estimate)'.
items.evidence: Triage said ABSENT, but flexible search of chapter-19.md finds all three fragments: 'the per-turn agent step averages ~120 ms for a 10,000-token context' (average), '$\lambda_\text{tool} \approx 100$ ms (median, tool backend)' (median; also table row 'Tool latency (median) | ~100 ms'), and 'So per-turn orchestration overhead *L*agent ≈ 220 ms (median)' (median). 120+100=220, so a stated average plus a stated median is labeled a median; median(X+Y) ≠ median(X)+median(Y) in general.

items.issue: The description says 'prefill + decode' (excluding tool), but the stated range 3.0–3.1 s matches the marginal cost INCLUDING the tool leg (2.94, 3.04, 3.14 s for turns 1–3). Prefill + decode only gives 2.80, 2.91, 3.01 s — a range of 2.8–3.0 s, not 3.0–3.1 s. Additionally, the range 3.0–3.1 does not cover turn 1's marginal cost (2.94 s with tool, 2.80 s without).

items.evidence: Flexible hit in chapter-19.md: 'the model's own per-turn work, prefill of the grown prefix + decode of *γ*, is carried inside *W*, ≈ 3.0–3.1 s marginal per turn'. Recomputed marginal per-turn cost from the ledger's inputs (10,065 / 10,930 / 11,795 at 9,200 tok / 1.08 s prefill): prefill+decode only = 1.182+1.625=2.81, 1.283+1.625=2.91, 1.385+1.625=3.01 → range 2.8–3.0 s, not 3.0–3.1. The stated range also excludes turn 1 (2.94 with tool, 2.81 without).

items.page_hint: Ch 19 §6, 'Inference scaling' paragraph, sentence beginning 'Agentic traffic is structurally more prefill-heavy'
items.issue: The ratio 0.14 → 0.40 is correct if defined as prefill_time/decode_time (1.08/7.5 = 0.144; 4.93/12.375 = 0.398). However, the term 'prefill/decode ratio' is not defined at this point, and the parenthetical '(1 → T+1 = 4 prefills per request)' suggests a count ratio (1 prefill vs 4 prefills) rather than a time ratio. A reader who interprets 'ratio' as a count (1/2 = 0.5 single-shot; 4/8 = 0.5 at T=3) will be confused by the 0.14 and 0.40 values.
items.quoted_clause: the prefill/decode ratio rises from ≈0.14 single-shot to ≈0.40 at T=3 (1 → T+1 = 4 prefills per request)
items.fix_instruction: In Ch 19, name the metric at first use ("the prefill-time/decode-time ratio rises from ≈0.14 (1.08 s / 7.5 s) to ≈0.40 (4.93 s / 12.375 s)") so the values and the count parenthetical are not conflated.
items.evidence: Quote found verbatim in design/manuscript/chapter-19/chapter-19.md: "Agentic traffic is structurally more prefill-heavy — the prefill/decode ratio rises from ≈0.14 single-shot to ≈0.40 at T=3 (1 → T+1 = 4 prefills per request)". Grep 'prefill/decode ratio' book-wide: exactly 1 occurrence (this sentence) — the term is never defined; every other 'prefill/decode' hit (ch2, ch11, ch12...) is the prefill/decode *split/disaggregation*, a different concept. Under a **100% prefix-reuse** policy only the incremental prefix (9,200 + 3×800 = 11,600 — the γ reasoning tokens were generated in the prior call, so their KV already exists) is pre-filled

items.issue: Two problems. (a) The mini-case mixes two populations without labelling: 4.47× and 1.29× are T = 3 figures (42,485/9,500 and 12,290/9,500), while the Lesson's 2.52× is the distribution-weighted per-submitted-request figure — the reader sees "4.47× → 1.29×" and "2.52×" in the same mini-case with no indication that they describe different populations. (b) "KV residency unchanged" is true of prefix caching but false of compaction, which the same sentence names as an alternative; compaction is precisely the lever that reduces the resident context.

(b) **processed model tokens** across all invocations grow ~152% per submitted request (2.52×, from the distribution-weighted 100-request ledger: 23,927 / 9,500)
items.fix_instruction: In Ch 19 §8 tag every multiplier with its population (T = 3 for 4.47×/1.29×, distribution-weighted for 2.52×), and split the Architectural-actions sentence so 'KV residency unchanged' attaches to prefix caching only; state what compaction does to residency.
items.evidence: Both segments EXACT in chapter-19.md §8 (Architectural actions at offset 48811, Lesson at 50169, both inside §8 which starts at 41834) despite _triage=ABSENT: 'adds prefix caching (or compaction) for the grown prefix — billed 4.47× → ≈1.29× and W 17.70 s → 14.16 s at 100% reuse, KV residency unchanged' and '(b) **processed model tokens** across all invocations grow ~152% per submitted request (2.52×, from the distribution-weighted 100-request ledger: 23,927 / 9,500)'. Populations verified: 42,485 = 'Processed (no prefix reuse)' T=3 (41,990+495), 42,485/9,500 = 4.47 ✓; 12,290 = 'Processed (100% prefix reuse)' T=3, 12,290/9,500 = 1.29 ✓; 23,927 = distribution-weighted ledger, /9,500 = 2.52 ✓ — the Architectural-actions sentence gives no T=3 tag (only 'The team sets the turn limit to 3' contextually) while 2.52× is tagged. Claim (b) verified: the sentence names 'prefix caching (or compaction)' and asserts 'KV residency unchanged' — compaction compresses the grown prefix and so changes KV residency, a property only prefix caching has.

The widely cited 236B MoE total (DeepSeek-V2/V3 lineage) uses 256 routed experts plus a shared expert with top-8 routing; the eight-expert, top-2 configuration is the Mixtral lineage, whose total is ~47B. (b) Precision absent ✓: "runs in ~18 GB" states no precision; arithmetic: 29.6B at 4-bit = 14.8 GB; 18 GB ÷ 29.6B = 0.608 B = 4.86 ≈ 4.9 bits/param — the figure is not reproducible as printed.

items.page_hint: Ch 3 §1, final paragraph of the Concept section ('A note on provenance') (printed page not determinable from chunk)
items.issue: This paragraph is about dense-vs-MoE training, but it is stranded at the end of the diffusion/LLaDA block, separated from the dense/MoE discussion it belongs to by roughly 1,500 words of unrelated material. It reads as a conclusion to the diffusion section, which it is not.
items.quoted_clause: "A note on provenance: the total-versus-active distinction arises from the training regime. In dense pre-training, every token sees the full model gradient; in MoE pre-training, a routing loss directs each token to the most relevant expert(s), and the unused experts receive no gradient for that step."
items.fix_instruction: Move the provenance paragraph to immediately after the two dense/MoE bullets in §1 (before the '### Alternative inference' subsection), or fold it into the §2 Mental Model MoE bullet; if it stays at the end of §1, retitle it so it does not read as a diffusion-section conclusion.
items.evidence: chapter-03.md: the paragraph 'A note on provenance: the total-versus-active distinction arises from the training regime. In dense pre-training...' sits immediately before '## 2. items.issue: The caption says the pipeline is 'in three bands' and then refers to 'The three bands and the single PERSISTENT KV CACHE box'. Visually there are two process bands (PREFILL and DECODE) plus one central cache box, not three bands plus a box.
items.fix_instruction: In the Fig 2.1 caption (chapter-02.md:21), make the count match the drawing: either label the cache region as the third band ('PREFILL / persistent cache / DECODE') or restate 'two process bands plus the persistent KV-cache box'; rebuild and verify the caption's count against the rendered figure.
items.evidence: page_035: two labelled band containers 'PREFILL' and 'DECODE' plus a separate 'PERSISTENT KV CACHE' box (vision); caption (pdftotext p.35) claims 'in three bands' and 'The three bands and the single PERSISTENT KV CACHE box are conceptual groupings' — the drawn grouping (2 bands + box) does not match the caption's count.

items.issue: The three panels of the continuous lane are drawn with essentially the same bar pattern, so the 'noise prior' panel is not visually distinguishable from the 'clean diffusion data' panel. The forward direction (data -> partly corrupted -> noise) is therefore not readable from the drawing; the reader must rely on the arrow labels and the caption to know which end is noise. As rendered, the figure does not show the corruption progression it describes.
items.fix_instruction: Redraw lane A so the progression reads at print size (smooth/structured bars for clean, visibly intermediate corruption, equal-magnitude or high-variance noise for the noise prior), or add a lane-A note stating the bars are schematic and the panels differ only schematically.
items.evidence: Zoomed look at panel A on page_051: the three bar patterns are different arrangements (tall bars at different positions), so 'near-identical' overstates it, but all three read as similar jagged texture — 'clean' is not smooth, 'noise prior' is not strikingly noisier, 'partly corrupted' does not read as an intermediate — so the data -> corrupted -> noise progression is not readable from the drawing, and lane A has no note.

items.figure: FIGURE 3.4 — right column legend and per-token line
items.issue: The symbol '11.4' denotes two different quantities in the figure body: GB-per-expert in the legend ('inactive experts ≈ 68 GB (6 × 11.4)', 'active experts ≈ 23 GB resident (2 × 11.4)') but billion-params-per-TWO-experts in the per-token line ('11.4B top-2'). The per-expert param count (5.7B) appears only in the caption, not the figure, so a reader cannot reconcile the two 11.4s from the figure alone.
items.fix_instruction: In the figure body state '1 expert = 5.7B params ≈ 11.4 GB (FP16)' and write the per-token line as 'top-2 = 11.4B (2 × 5.7B)', so the GB/expert and B/top-2 uses of 11.4 are reconcilable from the figure alone.
items.evidence: page_066 figure legend prints 'inactive experts ≈ 68 GB (6 × 11.4)' and 'active experts ≈ 23 GB resident (2 × 11.4)' (11.4 = GB per expert) while the per-token line prints 'per token: 11.4B top-2 + 1.4B always-on = 12.8B → 25.6 GB' (11.4B = params of two experts); the bridging 5.7B appears only in the caption (chapter-03.md line 207: '~11.4B = 2 × 5.7B'), so the same numeral carries two quantities in the figure alone.

items.issue: Terminology mismatch between caption and figure on the specialist group. Caption: "Each specialized family is a leaf the router can dispatch to" (plural families, each a leaf). Figure: a single bracket labelled "specialist family (one selected)" containing three leaves (Embedding, Vision, Math/reason). The figure says one family with three members; the caption says several families. A reader cannot tell whether Embedding/Vision/Math-reason are three families or three members of one family.
items.fix_instruction: Pick one term: change the figure group label to 'specialist models (one selected)' in render/fig_ch18_routing.py, or change chapter-18.md:206 to 'Each specialized model is a leaf...'; regenerate and re-read both strings on the rendered page.
items.evidence: Page 333 vision: group label 'specialist family (one selected)' over the three blue leaves vs text 'Each specialized family is a leaf the router can dispatch to' (chapter-18.md:206) - the figure treats the three leaves as members of one family, the text as three families.

items.figure: FIGURE 19.2 — Agent turns: token and KV growth (panel b)
items.issue: Panel (b) does not state the conversion constant that produces its numbers. The reader sees 9,500 tokens in panel (a) and 24.9 GB in panel (b) with no in-figure indication of the 2.62 MB/token (FP16) factor, so the figure's central claim (tokens -> KV) is not self-checking; the constant appears only in the caption and in Ch 19 prose.
items.fix_instruction: In render/fig_ch19_trend.py append ' at 2.62 MB/token (FP16)' to the panel (b) title (or add a one-line note), regenerate via the regen pipeline, and confirm the constant is visible on page 347.
items.evidence: Page 347 vision reads the whole figure: '2.62 MB/token' appears in no title, axis, legend, note or caption (grep chapter-19.md:222 caption also lacks it; fig_ch19_trend.py uses kv_mb=2.62 only for computation), so panel (b)'s 24.9->34.0 GB cannot be checked in-figure, while Fig 19.3's subtitle does carry the constant.

items.figure: Figure 26.1 — Workload fingerprints on the six axes
items.issue: The legend swatches are solid color blocks, while the bars use hatch patterns (diagonal, crosshatch, dots). In grayscale, the solid legend swatches collapse to similar gray values and do not carry the pattern encoding used in the plot, so the legend cannot reliably map categories to bars without color.
items.fix_instruction: In render/fig_ch26_fingerprint.py, make each legend swatch carry its series' hatch (draw the legend handles with the same hatch, or direct-label the three bars in every group) and re-render so swatch patterns match the bars.
items.evidence: Pixel measurement on page_425.png legend row (y1000-1012): blue swatch interior 133px with 0 dark pixels (solid), green swatch 0 (solid), orange 18 (marked) while the bars carry '/', 'x' and '.' hatches (vision + source fig_ch26_fingerprint.py:21-23) - the legend drops the pattern channel for 2 of 3 series, so in grayscale a reader cannot map swatch to bar by pattern.
